scope: Reduce exact custom sofa generation latency while retaining Argon, original object identity, editable parts and structural validation. Local only.

integrations.purpose: Generate an editable smart sofa with iron base and ESP32 without a full repeated JSON rewrite

checks.expected: Record a bounded same-prompt baseline, with original generator.
checks.observed: Original generator completed the exact prompt in 149.782s; first completed part at21.464s; actual Priority Argon;14 parts/180 solids/13336 output tokens. This is a single live baseline.

checks.expected: Bounded geometry recipes preserve solids, reject expansion bombs; schema defaults and targeted repairs validated; existing suite and production build pass.
checks.observed: 243 local/mock tests pass;3 opt-in live suites skipped in default run. Standalone typecheck and production build also pass. A separate live exact-prompt API test passed in78.214 seconds.

checks.expected: Exact smart sofa prompt finishes, contains distinct iron base and ESP32 parts, validates, and shows clickable parts in local UI.
checks.observed: The final browser Create form completed the same sofa prompt via Priority Argon in87.072 seconds. Its exported bytes validate:15 parts,254 solids,19 relationships,6 steps. Separate iron frame and ESP32 components; ESP32 independently selected. See actual project and screenshots. A previous failed browser attempt is recorded, not counted as a successful generation.

checks.expected: Malformed generation, repair failure, deadline and cancellation fail without replacing current object; no full second regeneration for a small structural defect.
checks.observed: Mocked targeted-reference repair keeps the geometry and emits one generation reset; exhausted repairs/malformed output/cancellation fail without a sample fallback. Recipe tests reject expansion bombs and unsafe repair paths.
